title_ar: شرح ورقات إمام الحرمين في أصول الفقه الشريط الأول
title_en: Commentary on the Waraqāt of Imam al-Haramayn on legal theory — tape one
body_ar:
بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم ، الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين.

هذا شرح ورقات إمام الحرمين في أصول الفقه وهو تأليف صغير مختصر للتعريفات المبدئية في أصول الفقه وضعه إمام الشافعية أبو المعالي عبد الملك بن عبد الله بن يوسف بن محمد الجويني نسبة إلى جوينة من نيسابور وقد ولد رحمه سنة 419هـ وتوفي سنة 478هـ ، وكان من مشاهير المتكلمين والفقهاء والأصوليين وقد ألف هذه الورقات لتكون مبدءا لطلاب العلم يعرفون به بعض مصطلحات أصول الفقه ، وأصول الفقه علم من أهم العلوم الشرعية لأنه الذي يمكن أن يتوصل به إلى فهم الكتاب والسنة و أخذ الأحكام منهما ، و ذلك أن الكتاب والسنة يبحث فيهما من جهتين ـ جهة الورود وجهة الدلالة ، أما جهة الورود فهي النقل بمعنى التحقق من ثبوت نسبة القرآن إلى الله والتحقق من ثبوت نسبة الحديث إلى النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وذلك بالرواية والإسناد والجهة الثانية ، جهة الدلالة ومعناها ما يراد بهذا الكلام ، ما يريده الله من عباده بهذا اللفظ ، وما يريده النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم من أمته بهذا اللفظ .
body_en:
In the name of God, the Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I pray for blessing and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and all who are guided by his guidance and follow his sunnah until the Day of Judgement.

This is the commentary on the Waraqāt of Imam al-Haramayn on legal theory. It is a small, abridged composition of the introductory definitions in legal theory, set down by the imam of the Shafi'is, Abu al-Maʿali ʿAbd al-Malik ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Yusuf ibn Muhammad al-Juwayni — the name being taken from Juwaynah, of Nishapur. He was born, may God have mercy on him, in the year 419 AH and died in the year 478 AH, and he was among the famous theologians, jurists and legal theorists. He composed these Waraqāt so that they might be a beginning for students of knowledge, by which they would come to know some of the terms of legal theory.

Legal theory is among the most important of the Sharia sciences, because it is that by which one can arrive at an understanding of the Book and the sunnah, and at the taking of rulings from them. That is because the Book and the sunnah are investigated from two sides: the side of their coming down, and the side of their signification. As for the side of their coming down, it is transmission — meaning the ascertaining of the attribution of the Qur'an to God, and the ascertaining of the attribution of the hadith to the Prophet, upon whom be God's blessing and peace; and that is by narration and by the chain of transmission. And the second side, the side of signification, means what is intended by this speech: what God wants from His servants by this wording, and what the Prophet, upon whom be God's blessing and peace, wants from his community by this wording.

flags.note: The place from which al-Juwayni takes his name is normally given as Juwayn, a district in the region of Nishapur. The source prints Juwaynah. This is either a transcription of how the Sheikh said it or a slip; it is translated as printed under the rule against silently repairing the source. The birth and death years the Sheikh gives, 419 and 478 AH, are both as standardly reported.

This record belongs to the Sheikh's commentary on al-Waraqāt of Imam al-Haramayn al-Juwayni, a short primer on legal theory. The CMS holds the tapes out of order across ids 649–652 and the tape numbers in the titles do not run with the ids; the series should be ordered by the tape number in the title, not by id, and tape two does not appear anywhere in the range 601–652.

EXCERPT ONLY. The published text breaks off and the full material is offered as a .docx download ('taḥmīl al-māddah'). The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. The download-link label has been removed from body_ar as a navigation element and recorded in source_download_link.
'Imam al-Haramayn' — the imam of the two sanctuaries, Mecca and Medina — is al-Juwayni's title and is kept as the name by which the book is known.
'Theologians' renders mutakallimūn, the practitioners of kalām, speculative theology. It should not be read as a general word for religious scholars; the Sheikh is listing three distinct specialisms.

The distinction between the 'side of coming down' (wurūd, i.e. whether a text is authentically transmitted) and the 'side of signification' (dalālah, i.e. what it means) is the organising distinction of the whole discipline, and the English keeps the two labels sharply apart.
The record ends on a completed sentence and poses no unanswered question, so it is not marked critical_for_display, although it is only the opening of the lecture.
